courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Ancient to Medieval Art
courses.description: [IAI Code: F2901] Development of the visual arts in Western Europe and the Near East in their cultural contexts from prehistoric times until the early fifteenth century; includes Egyptian, Greek, Roman, and medieval art and architecture.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: The Middle Ages in Popular Culture
courses.description: Explores the use of medievalism in contemporary popular culture. Instructors may draw from film, television, music, fiction, graphic novels, gaming, and other sources, and they approach the material from a variety of cultural, historical, and aesthetic traditions. The goal of the course will be to understand how the medieval periods of world cultures have been reinvented in modern times, and how modernity has been constructed in relation and in opposition to the medieval imaginary.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval Literature and Culture
courses.description: Introduction to the diverse literatures and cultures of the global Middle Ages (approximately 500-1500 CE). Students will read works by medieval authors in Modern English translation, with particular attention to placing works in their historical and material contexts.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the Composition I requirement.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 253 and ENGL 202. See ENGL 202.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Legends of King Arthur
courses.description: Arthurian myth and legend is one of the most enduring literary traditions of Western Europe, and the characters of Arthur, Merlin, Guinevere, Lancelot, Gawain and Mordred were as popular in the Middle Ages as they are today. Originating in early medieval Wales, the legends traveled through England to France and Germany and throughout the modern world. Students will study the development of the Arthurian tradition in chronicles, poetry, romances, lais, and fabliaux, comparing variations across cultural and historical boundaries.
courses.prereqText: Completion of the Composition I requirement.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 216 and ENGL 216. See ENGL 216.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval Art
courses.description: The arts of Byzantium and Western Europe from the early Christian era to the Renaissance.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Northern Renaissance Art
courses.description: Architecture, painting, sculpture, and minor arts of Europe outside Italy in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Italy Middle Ages & Renaiss
courses.description: The development of Medieval Italian civilization in a literary context from the Sicilian School of love poetry to the early Renaissance in Florence; lectures and readings are in English.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 240 and ITAL 240. See ITAL 240.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Wives, Workers and Witches in Pre-Modern Europe
courses.description: Examines the history of women and the evolution of concepts of gender in western Europe from roughly 400 to 1700. Topics include the interactions of class and ethnicity with women's experiences, the social construction of sexuality and gender, the misogynist tradition, and women's self-images.
courses.pointerText: Same as GWS 245 and HIST 245. See HIST 245.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval Europe
courses.description: From the fragmentation of the Roman Empire to the formation of territorial monarchies, this course surveys the events, innovations, crises, and movements that shaped western Europe in a pivotal era known as "the Middle Ages." Topics will include the spread of Christianity, the migration of peoples, fundamental changes in economic and social structures, the development of political institutions, the role of women, and the cultural achievements of different communities (the monastery, the town, the court).

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Viking Mythology
courses.description: Studies pre-Christian beliefs of the Germanic peoples as reflected primarily in medieval Icelandic prose and poetry (in translation).
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 251, REL 251, and SCAN 251. See SCAN 251.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Viking Sagas in Translation
courses.description: [IAI Code: H9901] Studies Old Norse-Icelandic literature: kings' sagas, family sagas, mythical-heroic sagas, and romances. Texts and lectures in English.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 252 and SCAN 252. See SCAN 252.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: British Isles to 1688
courses.description: Survey of the political, social and economic, religious, and cultural history of the British people from the "prehistoric" era through the revolution of 1688.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Jewish Intellectual History: Encounters with Islam and Christianity
courses.description: Study of the distinctive religious ideas, movements, and figures of pre-Modern Judaism [500 CE-1700 CE] with an emphasis on how Judaism’s encounter with medieval Islam and Christianity influenced these new Jewish expressions. Topics include theology, philosophy, Biblical interpretation, mysticism, Jewish-Christian polemics, and law.
courses.pointerText: Same as JS 344 and REL 344. See REL 344.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval Civilization
courses.description: The architectural, artistic, philosophical, political, and religious components of medieval culture, thought, and patterns of behavior; includes monasticism and society and the individual.
courses.pointerText: Same as HIST 345 and REL 345. See HIST 345.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: The Age of the Renaissance
courses.description: An introduction to the cultural history of Europe in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, embracing the Renaissance movements in Italy and in Northern Europe.
courses.pointerText: Same as HIST 346 and REL 346. See HIST 346.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Introduction to Old English
courses.description: Introduction to the form of English spoken and written prior to about AD 1100. Exploring concepts of cultural, historical, and linguistic change, students will learn to read Old English texts in the original. Readings include examples from the prose tradition (e.g., Bede's story of the poet Cædmon and Ælfric's Lives of Saints) as well as poetic texts (e.g., The Dream of the Rood and The Wanderer). 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Topics in Medieval British and Irish Literature
courses.description: Advanced topics course exploring the literatures of medieval Britain and Ireland, concentrating on texts in Old and/or Middle English but with some attention to Celtic, French, Latin, and Norse texts in translation. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated with permission of English advising office to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours if topics vary; Graduate students may repeat if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: One year of college literature or consent of instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 417 and ENGL 412. See ENGL 412.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Chaucer
courses.description: A selection of Chaucer's major works read in Middle English. Instructors will usually emphasize either the Canterbury Tales or Troilus and Criseyde and the dream visions, but alternate combinations of texts are possible. Students will also be introduced to Chaucer's fourteenth-century context. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: One year of college literature or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval Architecture
courses.description: Introduces the architecture, monumental arts, and urbanism of Byzantium and medieval western Europe from c. 300-1500, using a comparative approach. We will learn about Byzantium’s domed churches and robust cities, Europe’s Romanesque monasteries and pilgrimage destinations, and its soaring Gothic cathedrals, fortresses, and cities. It integrates architecture with the study of the roles of secular and ecclesiastical authority, design and technological developments, religious performance and observance, warfare and trade between regions, and developing urbanism. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: ARCH 210 or ARTH 111.
courses.pointerText: Same as ARCH 412 and ARTH 412. See ARCH 412.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Dante
courses.description: Interpretation of Dante's Divine Comedy with special attention to its position in the medieval world; a knowledge of Italian not required. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 413 and ITAL 413. See ITAL 413.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Petrarch & Boccaccio
courses.description: Studies in Petrarch and Boccaccio; nonmajors in Italian may read the works in translation; lectures are in English. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Fulfillment of campus rhetoric requirement.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 414 and ITAL 414. See ITAL 414.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Topics in the History of Romance Languages
courses.description: Introduction to the analysis of primary sources on the historical development of individual Romance languages from their Latin origins to the present. Examination of a variety of genres and media and the social role of the languages in the definition of national identities. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated in the same or separate terms to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Approval by instructor.
courses.pointerText: Same as FR 417 and RMLG 417. See FR 417.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Masterpieces Renaiss Lit
courses.description: Reading of masterpieces of the 1400 and 1500s and a study of their predecessors and influence; nonconcentrators in Italian may read the works in translation; lectures are in English. Content rotates. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours with consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Fulfillment of campus rhetoric requirement.
courses.pointerText: Same as CWL 420 and ITAL 420. See ITAL 420.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Romanesque Art
courses.description: Art and architecture of the Romanesque period. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Gothic Art
courses.description: Arts of western Europe from the end of the Romanesque period until the Renaissance. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Topics: Northern Art 1300-1500
courses.description: Special topics in the history of painting, sculpture, and minor arts of France, Germany, Spain, and England during the Renaissance selected for intensive study. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Fifteenth-Century Italian Art
courses.description: Study of Italian painting, sculpture and architecture from circa 1300 to 1500. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Early Christian Thought
courses.description: Study of major developments in early Christian thought (first four centuries) through discussion of primary texts in translation. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: REL 121 or REL 202, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Byzantine Empire AD 284-717
courses.description: Examination of the political, social, economic, military, institutional, religious and cultural development of the early Byzantine Empire from the reign of Diocletian (AD 284-305) through the Heraclian Dynasty (AD 610-717). 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval England
courses.description: Key sources and topics of English history, from the end of Roman rule in Britain (c. 410) to the fifteenth century. Recurrent themes include the development of law, the role of women, the status of commoners, intellectual trends, and the importance of public media for the dissemination of ideas (writing, performance). 3 undergraduate hours. 2 or 4 graduate hours.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval Latin
courses.description: Literary and historical texts in prose and poetry will be read in the original; the course will also cover patristic writings. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Two years of college Latin or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Middle Ages to Baroque
courses.description: Literary, thematic, cultural, and bibliographical analysis of the major authors, works, genres, and movements in German literature from 750-1720. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours. May be repeated in separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Seminar in Medieval Studies
courses.description: Team-taught, interdisciplinary seminar on varying topics in Medieval Studies drawing on faculty from UIUC and invited scholars from other universities. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Genesis in History
courses.description: Survey of Jewish and Christian cultural reception of Genesis in the ancient and medieval worlds. Examines techniques of exegesis and strategies of interpretation in the ancient world, such as allegory, narrative expansion, and retelling. Engages with foundational studies of modern scholarship on biblical reception. While focusing on the initial chapters of Genesis, we will also explore the appropriation of Abraham traditions and the Joseph story.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Old Norse-Icelandic I
courses.description: Grammar and selected readings. Offered in alternate years.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Old Norse-Icelandic II
courses.description: Readings; selections from the Elder Edda and the sagas. Offered in alternate years.
courses.prereqText: SCAN 505.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Seminar in Medieval Architecture
courses.description: Seminar on topics in medieval architecture and urbanism. Course Information: May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours in separate terms. Course Information:
courses.prereqText: ARCH 411, ARCH 412, or equivalent as determined by the instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Seminar in Medieval Literature
courses.description: Intensive study of selected texts, genres, themes, or theoretical issues in medieval British literature (usually focusing on either Old English or Middle English texts), or of scholarly methods in medieval studies (such as editing, paleography, or bibliography and methods of historical research). May be repeated in separate terms up to 12 hours, if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: A college course devoted entirely to an aspect of medieval studies or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Seminar in Medieval Art
courses.description: Research seminar in subjects selected from the art and architecture of the medieval period. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Old High German
courses.description: Grammar and interpretation of the oldest literary documents.
courses.prereqText: GER 465.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Seminar in N. Renaissance Art
courses.description: Research seminar in subjects selected from the art of the Northern Renaissance. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Problems in Medieval History
courses.description: Topics will be listed in the department's course guide at http://www.history.illinois.edu. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Research Seminar: Medieval
courses.description: Topics will be listed in the department's course guide at https://www.history.illinois.edu. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Seminar Old French Literature
courses.description: Discussion and research on a specialized topic in Old French literature. See Schedule for current topic. May be repeated.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MDVL
courses.title: Medieval German Studies
courses.description: Seminar in selected genres, themes, or authors of the Middle Ages. Epic, lyric, and didactic works in prose and verse are read in the original language. May be repeated to a maximum of 12 hours if topics vary.
